Maximum sustained wind.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Maximum sustained wind.question: The _____ was Intensity indicator of tropical cyclone.
Maximum sustained wind.fact: The maximum sustained wind associated with a tropical cyclone is a common indicator of the intensity of the storm. Wind measuring has been standardized globally to reflect the winds at 10 meters (33 ft) above mean sea level, and the maximum sustained wind represents the highest average wind over either a one-minute (US) or ten-minute time span (see the definition, below), anywhere within the tropical cyclone.

Maximum sustained wind.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Maximum sustained wind.question: Surface winds are highly variable due to friction between the atmosphere and the _____'s surface, as well as near hills and mountains over land
Maximum sustained wind.fact: Surface winds are highly variable due to friction between the atmosphere and the Earth's surface, as well as near hills and mountains over land.

Maximum sustained wind.question: This value helps determine the damage potential of a tropical cyclone, through use of such scales as the Saffir–_____ scale
Maximum sustained wind.fact: This value helps determine the damage potential of a tropical cyclone, through use of such scales as the Saffir–Simpson scale.

Maximum sustained wind.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Maximum sustained wind.question: However, the _____ defines sustained winds within tropical cyclones by averaging winds over a period of one minute, measured at the same 10 meters (33 ft) height
Maximum sustained wind.fact: However, the United States National Weather Service defines sustained winds within tropical cyclones by averaging winds over a period of one minute, measured at the same 10 meters (33 ft) height.

Maximum sustained wind.subject: Meteorology & Climate
Maximum sustained wind.question: In the _____ and northeast Pacific oceans, the Saffir–Simpson scale is used
Maximum sustained wind.fact: In the Atlantic and northeast Pacific oceans, the Saffir–Simpson scale is used.

Maximum sustained wind.question: Most weather agencies use the definition for sustained winds recommended by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), which specifies measuring winds at a height of _____ (33 ft) for 10 minutes, an
Maximum sustained wind.fact: Most weather agencies use the definition for sustained winds recommended by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO), which specifies measuring winds at a height of 10 meters (33 ft) for 10 minutes, and then taking the average. However, the United States National Weather Service defines sustained winds within tropical cyclones by averaging winds over a period of one minute, measured at the same 10 meters (33 ft) height.

However, the United States National Weather Service defines sustained winds within tropical cyclones by averaging winds over a period of one minute, measured at the same 10 meters (33 ft) height.
